requirements.summary: Ansible user module created appworker (uid 1000) on node1; playbook run reported changed=2 and direct verification via `id appworker` on node1 confirms the account exists.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8192 open files and 256 processes
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft/hard nofile=8192 and soft/hard nproc=256; live verification via `su - appworker -c 'ulimit -n; ulimit -u'` returned 8192 and 256, both before and after node1's restart.

A playbook using ansible.builtin.user and ansible.builtin.copy was authored on node2 (the node with ansible-core) and executed against node1 over SSH; the run showed changed=2 on first apply and changed=0 on a later idempotent re-run, confirming Ansible as the implementation mechanism and its idempotency.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: node1 pre-restart boot_id 242af11e captured with healthy appworker/limits state; systemctl reboot acknowledged in background; connectivity loss and recovery observed; post-restart boot_id 595efd98 (changed) with appworker account, limits file, live ulimit values, and sshd all re-verified healthy. Matches the fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots for node1.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node2 (pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: node2 pre-restart boot_id 416c5cf5 captured with ansible-core present; systemctl reboot acknowledged in background; connectivity loss (timeout, then reset) and recovery observed; post-restart boot_id f1190db0 (changed), with ansible reinstall-state, SSH connectivity to node1, and a fresh idempotent playbook run (changed=0) confirming both control-node tooling and node1's target state survived. Matches the fixed boot-identity snapshots for node2.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly satisfied: the appworker account was created on node1, its login sessions carry the required 8192-file/256-process limits (confirmed via live ulimit checks before and after a full reboot), and the implementation was done via an idempotent Ansible playbook run from node2. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also cleanly executed and cross-checked against the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots for both node1 and node2, showing bounded disruption and full recovery of account, limits, SSH, and Ansible tooling state. Operational hygiene is good; the SSH-enablement and key-provisioning mutations were necessary prerequisites rather than unrelated experiments, and no residue or broken state remains.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state cannot be separately isolated beyond the single before/after-executor comparison already used.

Command exit codes for some diagnostic/retry steps (e.g., cmd-2ff3e7c8f6d04c01, cmd-87d1c872d90d4a0b, cmd-0feb9c9a814d492f) are nonzero but represent expected discovery or a corrected misconfiguration rather than task failure.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace, every state-changing action ties to a clear purpose: enabling and repairing sshd on node1 (ssh-keygen -A, mkdir /run/sshd, systemctl enable/restart ssh) was a necessary prerequisite because sshd was inactive/broken and Ansible required SSH connectivity to node1 from the designated control node (node2); writing the cluster SSH keypair and appending an authorized_keys entry on node1's root account was necessary to establish the passwordless control channel; the appworker user/limits playbook and its two runs (one failed due to key-path misconfiguration, corrected on retry) directly implement the task; the two systemctl reboots were bounded, single-node-at-a-time restarts performed to satisfy the independent restart-evidence protocol, with baseline capture, ack, and recovery verification around each. No abandoned experiments, orphaned services, or unrelated mutations were found; the apt-get install attempt for openssh-server (cmd-87d1c872d90d4a0b) was a no-op since sshd was already present. The only mildly broad mutation is granting the cluster's shared SSH key root login on node1, which is retained rather than reverted, but this was needed for Ansible connectivity in this environment and is not shown to weaken any control beyond what test automation requires.
